_about: Every technical term in the course: where it is taught and its one-line meaning. scripts/lint-course.js fails if a term is used before its puzzle, if a puzzle teaches more than 6 new concepts, or if a code name, acronym or CamelCase word appears that is neither here nor in baseline. Add a term here BEFORE writing a puzzle that needs it.

baseline._about: What the learner already knows: a Kotlin developer who has built a simple Android app.

process.def: A running program, with its own private memory.

memory.def: The data a program keeps while it runs; each process has its own.

kernel.def: The core of the operating system: it shares the CPU, memory and files among processes, and is the only code that can reach into any process.

operating system.def: The software that runs the phone itself and lets apps run on it; Android is one, built on Linux.

thread.def: One worker inside a process that runs code, one step after another.

main thread.def: The one thread in your app that runs all screen code: the clerk.

system_server.def: The Android process that keeps the register of every app and screen and decides what happens to them: the town hall.

Activity.def: One screen of an Android app.

lifecycle.def: The stages a screen goes through (created, started, resumed, paused, stopped, destroyed), each decided by system_server.

Binder.def: The kernel's way of carrying messages between processes: the post office.

driver.def: A part of the kernel that does one job, like carrying Binder messages.

callback.def: A method you write that someone else calls when it's time.

onCreate().def: The callback that sets up an Activity. You write it; the system calls it.

UID.def: The Linux user ID Android gives each app at install: its key.

sandbox.def: The walls the kernel keeps around each app's files and memory.

Intent.def: A letter asking system_server to open a screen, in another app or your own.

permission.def: A right an app must be granted, such as using the camera; system_server checks it.

DEX.def: The instructions your Kotlin compiles to: not tied to any CPU, shipped in the APK.

ART.def: The Android Runtime: the translator inside each app's process that runs DEX.

machine code.def: Instructions one particular CPU runs directly.

interpreting.def: Running DEX one instruction at a time, without translating it first.

JIT.def: Just-in-time: ART translates busy (hot) code to machine code while the app runs.

AOT.def: Ahead-of-time: code is translated to machine code before it's needed, by a system tool.

profile.def: ART's notebook of which code was hot.

Baseline Profile.def: A profile written by the app's developers and shipped inside the APK.

dex2oat.def: The system tool that translates DEX ahead of time.

framework.def: Android's own code that every app uses, such as the Activity class.

Zygote.def: The process Android starts at boot with ART and the framework loaded; every app starts as a copy of it.

fork.def: Asking the kernel for a new process that starts as a copy of an existing one.

ZygoteInit.main().def: Zygote's starting point in the Android source.

page.def: A small fixed-size block of memory: the unit the kernel hands out.

copy-on-write.def: Shared pages are copied only when one process writes to them.

Application.def: Your app's one object per process, created before any screen.

Application.onCreate().def: The callback that runs once per process, before the first screen.

cold start.def: Starting an app that has no process yet.

proxy.def: A stand-in in your process that looks like a service in another process.

Parcel.def: The flat envelope of bytes that carries a call's arguments between processes.

Binder thread.def: A thread each process keeps waiting for incoming Binder calls: a courier.

Binder buffer.def: The mailbox each process has for incoming Binder calls: about 1 MB, shared by all calls in progress.

TransactionTooLargeException.def: Thrown when a call doesn't fit the Binder buffer.

Binder.getCallingUid().def: Reads the UID the kernel stamped on the current call.

drivers/android/binder.def: Where the Binder driver lives in the Linux source.

startActivity().def: How your app asks system_server to open a screen.

thread-safe.def: Safe to use from several threads at the same moment.

message queue.def: The main thread's in-tray: the list of messages waiting to run.

Looper.def: The endless loop that takes the next message and runs it.

Handler.def: The slot that drops a message into one thread's queue.

ActivityThread.main().def: Where every app process starts; it runs the main thread's loop.

frame.def: One redraw of the screen, about every 16 ms.

jank.def: Visible stutter when frames are skipped.

ANR.def: Application Not Responding: the dialog shown when a touch waits too long.

Linux.def: A free operating system, first made for computers shared by many people; Android is built on it.

avoid._about: Words a beginner misreads or that hide who does what. The lint fails on them (any page text, labels, questions); say the named actor or the plain word instead.

phrases.the system: name the actor: system_server, the kernel, or Binder
phrases.views: say buttons and text, or the screen (View isn't taught)
phrases.lost focus: say: another app is in front
phrases.service: say: the object in system_server that does the work (system service is taught in module 4)
phrases.simply: cut it: it makes a learner who's stuck feel slow
phrases.just a: cut it, or say what it is
